source.check: returned unopposed: selected as the Unionist candidate for the division (Impartial Reporter, 27 April 1961, p. 6); the Reporter of 18 May 1961 (p. 7) reports the nominations, with Kinawley the only contest, and names the changes on Enniskillen Rural Council (Aghnaglack, Ballyreagh, Castlecoole, Florencecourt, Tempo); sat as a member of the new council (Impartial Reporter, 9 November 1961, p. 7; Impartial Reporter, 7 December 1961, p. 7)

note: Triennial election of Enniskillen Rural District Council, polled Thursday 1 June 1961. Kinawley was the only contested division in County Fermanagh; the uncontested divisions are not named in the reports read. The Belfast Telegraph of 31 May 1961, p. 2, confirms that Enniskillen Rural Council had 'one' contest, at Kinawley, 'where Mr. Charles McBarron (Nationalist) is being opposed by another Nationalist, Mr. Patrick McGovern'. Added 6 Nov 2026 from the Impartial Reporter: the five changes named in its nominations report of 18 May 1961 (p. 7) and the Unionist members re-selected for their divisions in its reports of 20 and 27 April and 4 and 11 May 1961; each was returned unopposed. Recorded for Nationalist-held divisions from the selection lists and first-meeting reports in the Fermanagh Herald: Holywell and Drumane. Recorded from reports of the new council's meetings during the term: Coolyermor, Clabby, Drumderg, Derrybrusk, Monea and Garvary. Returned unopposed.
